news.summary_en: Ramp AI Index and OpenRouter data indicate that US corporate AI usage is hitting record highs while the average cost per million tokens has dropped below $0.45 due to aggressive pricing competition. Anthropic has surpassed OpenAI in both spending and volume market share, signaling a paradigm shift in the AI infrastructure market from a high-premium phase to a defensive pricing cycle.
paragraphs: US companies are using AI models more intensively than ever and paying less for the privilege.

The latest update of the Ramp AI Index, which draws on transaction data from more than 85,000 US companies, lays out the numbers. Tokens, the units of computation in which AI providers bill model usage, got 21.2 percent cheaper in six weeks, according to Ramp lead economist Ara Kharazian. At the same time, token volume rose 1.5 percent to a record high.

Token spending, meaning what companies actually pay for AI APIs, fell 6.3 percent from its peak two weeks earlier. Month over month (the week ending November 15 vs. the week ending October 18), total token spending still rose 12 percent, but token volume jumped 27.2 percent over the same span. The gap between usage and revenue keeps widening.

The average price per million tokens for OpenAI and Anthropic combined fell to $0.45, according to Ramp, down 11.2 percent from the prior month. OpenAI is cheaper at $0.38 per million tokens compared with $0.50 for Anthropic.

API routing platform OpenRouter shows a similar pattern. According to an analysis Peter Walker published on X, weekly token volume for closed-weight models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google grew 1,215 percent since the start of 2026. Weekly spending rose 455 percent over the same period, far more slowly. The spending peak came in the week of October 5, according to the OpenRouter data, which runs through the week of November 9. Spending has been declining since then.

Ramp's token metrics rely on usage and billing data imported from AI providers, while OpenRouter measures traffic through its API routing platform. The fact that both sources show a spending peak in October followed by declining outlays and rising volume reinforces the trend, though neither service is representative of the overall market. OpenRouter in particular offers only a narrow window into a very specific user base.
### Anthropic dominates the token market on IPO day

In the week ending November 15, 2026, Anthropic accounted for 58.7 percent of all token spending, according to the Ramp AI Index, up 1.7 percentage points from the prior month. Its share of token volume was even higher at 59.4 percent. OpenAI fell to 37.2 percent of spending and 37.7 percent of volume. Google came in at 1.4 percent and xAI (SpaceXAI) at 2.4 percent.
Kharazian wrote on X that Anthropic holds this share on IPO day. In October, however, Anthropic's token spending grew only 0.5 percent month over month, while OpenAI's grew 2.1 percent.

In October 2026, 56.8 percent of all tracked US companies paid for AI products or services, according to Ramp, up one percentage point from September and 13.3 percentage points more than a year earlier. Anthropic leads with an adoption rate of 44.8 percent, while OpenAI sits at 40.6 percent.
### Stripe data also shows strong AI growth and signs of cooling

The Ramp AI Index tracks the demand side, what companies spend on AI. Payment processor Stripe has published its own AI Index that measures the supply side: incoming payments at roughly 20,000 AI companies that use Stripe.

According to the Stripe AI Index, revenue at AI companies grew 103 percent over the 52 weeks ending November 8. The typical (median) AI company grew only 41 percent, though, suggesting that a few large providers are skewing the overall picture.

The slowdown over shorter time frames is pronounced. Annualized over 13 weeks, growth stood at about 80 percent, down from 140 percent just a few months ago. The US leads with 104 percent year-over-year growth, while the EU sits at 67 percent. AI companies are growing far faster than traditional software firms, according to Stripe: 103 percent compared with 33 percent in the SaaS Index.

Both indexes paint a similar picture. AI is still growing fast, but momentum is cooling. At Ramp, that shows up through falling prices and concentrated demand. At Stripe, it shows up through slowing growth rates on the provider side.

New growth could emerge from more capable or more reliable models, or simply from better integration of current models into business workflows. The potential is there, considering how AI has upended the entire coding market in a matter of months. The AI industry still depends on extraordinarily strong growth, though, if it wants to recoup the massive capacity buildout it has planned.

news.author: Sarah Perez
news.content_snippet:
Google on Thursday announced that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background.

The tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time. Meanwhile, Google only this week announced the broader
news.summary_en: Google has introduced 'Computer Use' capabilities to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, enabling the AI agent to navigate native apps, manage local files, and browse the web on the user's behalf. This feature is gated behind Gemini Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscriptions and is currently limited to English users in the U.S., requiring explicit user approval for agentic actions via a live preview interface.
paragraphs: Google on Thursday announced that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background.

The tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time. Meanwhile, Google only this week announced the broader rollout of Gemini’s “Tasks,” the in-app feature that allows the AI to work more as an agent, helping users sign into websites, make online purchases, or book appointments.

Google also only recently began admitting early testers to try its revamped “CC” AI agent, announced in September, which is designed to help families stay organized across email, calendars, chats, and tasks.

Computer use is another type of agentic offering that allows an AI agent to take actions directly on the user’s computer — in Gemini’s case, a Mac. This allows the AI to complete multistep tasks that involve getting things done across local files, apps, and the web. After the user instructs the AI what they want to do, they’ll see the agent working in a live preview in their chat, while still keeping their screen and cursor free to continue working on other things.
As with other AI agents offering computer use, users can pause, stop, and approve Gemini’s actions before they happen.

Google suggests the feature could be useful for tedious tasks and other workflows, like filling out forms, repeating the same task over and over across a batch of files, organizing files into folders based on specific criteria, creating slideshows from files or information in online dashboards, and more.

The feature is initially available in English in the U.S. and requires the Gemini app for Mac and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription. The company didn’t say when it would expand to other markets or platforms.

celebrity.full_text_en:
I came across an interesting finding in yesterday’s @databricks announcement.

After studying more than 80,000 customer pipeline issues, the company found that over half required knowledge specific to the organization to resolve.

And I think there’s a much bigger business lesson hiding in that number.

When we talk about AI agents, we often focus on what they can do.

Can they write content?

Can they analyze data?

Can they manage workflows?

Can they complete tasks without constant human involvement?

Those are useful questions.

But there’s another one I find increasingly important as we build CAIS.

Does the agent actually understand the business it’s working for?

Imagine two companies using exactly the same AI tools.

One wants to increase sales as quickly as possible.

The other is prioritizing profitability, customer retention and protecting its brand positioning.

An agent might recommend the same aggressive discount campaign to both.

The recommendation could be technically sound.

But it wouldn’t necessarily be right for both businesses.

That’s the difference between having access to information and understanding business context.

It’s also why we’re building CAIS around the idea of One Brand Brain.

The goal is to bring business strategy, knowledge, people and AI workflows into a more coherent operating environment.

Not because every decision should be automated.

Quite the opposite.

Because businesses need to know which decisions can be delegated, which require additional context and which should remain firmly in human hands.

I think we’ll see increasingly capable agents over the coming months.

But capability alone won’t determine which businesses benefit most.

The companies that understand their own processes, priorities and decision-making responsibilities will be in a much stronger position to use that capability effectively.

Sometimes the most valuable thing you can give an AI agent isn’t another tool.

It’s a better understanding of the business.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
我在昨天的@databricks 公告中发现了一个有趣的发现。

在研究了 80,000 多个客户渠道问题后，该公司发现超过一半的问题需要组织特有的知识来解决。

我认为这个数字中隐藏着更大的商业教训。

当我们谈论人工智能代理时，我们经常关注它们能做什么。

他们可以写内容吗？

他们可以分析数据吗？

他们可以管理工作流程吗？

它们能否在没有人类持续参与的情况下完成任务？

这些都是有用的问题。

但我发现，随着我们建立 CAIS，还有一个问题变得越来越重要。

代理人是否真正了解其所从事的业务？

想象一下两家公司使用完全相同的人工智能工具。

人们希望尽快增加销售额。

另一个是优先考虑盈利能力、客户保留和保护其品牌定位。

代理商可能会向两者推荐相同的激进折扣活动。

该建议在技术上可能是合理的。

但这不一定适合两家企业。

这就是获取信息和了解业务环境之间的区别。

这也是我们围绕同一个品牌大脑的理念构建 CAIS 的原因。

目标是将业务战略、知识、人员和人工智能工作流程带入一个更加一致的操作环境中。

并不是因为每个决定都应该自动化。

恰恰相反。

因为企业需要知道哪些决策可以委托，哪些需要额外的背景信息，哪些应该牢牢掌握在人手中。

我认为在接下来的几个月里我们会看到能力越来越强的特工。

但仅凭能力并不能决定哪些企业受益最多。

了解自己的流程、优先事项和决策责任的公司将能够更有效地利用这种能力。

有时，你能为人工智能代理提供的最有价值的东西并不是其他工具。

这是对业务的更好理解。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Fewer than 100 people worldwide are known to have this extraordinary condition.

A rare instance of hyperthymesia—also called highly superior autobiographical memory (HSAM)—offers a striking glimpse into how the human brain can construct a vivid, structured, and navigable mental landscape of a lifetime's experiences.

Picture entering a mental "white room" where every personal moment is meticulously archived: memories filed in binders by theme, chronology, and emotional tone, or visualized as photographs and text messages on shelves. For a 17-year-old French high-school student referred to as TL, this is her everyday experience—not a metaphor, but a controlled cognitive reality.

TL, one of the fewer than 100 documented cases of hyperthymesia, can voluntarily "re-experience" past events with full sensory detail, often from multiple perspectives, and even choose to compartmentalize difficult memories (such as sealing painful ones away in a mental chest) while shifting focus to calmer "rooms" to regulate emotions like anger.

What sets TL apart is her ability to also "pre-experience" future scenarios with comparable vividness and emotional richness—a capacity known as episodic future thinking. This allows her to mentally simulate upcoming personal events as if they are already unfolding.

Researchers describe her memory system as a sophisticated, self-organized architecture that she accesses at will, providing exceptional voluntary control over autobiographical recall—unlike many others with hyperthymesia who find their memories intrusive or overwhelming.

By studying TL's unique case, scientists gain valuable insight into the neural mechanisms of mental time travel: the ability to flexibly revisit the past and project into the future. This reveals memory not merely as passive storage, but as a dynamic, spatially and emotionally structured framework that shapes personal identity and our sense of continuity across time.

The findings, detailed in a 2025 case study, highlight how such exceptional cognitive organization may deepen our understanding of human consciousness and autobiographical memory.

[La Corte, V., Piolino, P., & Cohen, L. (2025). Autobiographical hypermnesia as a particular form of mental time travel. Neurocase. Advance online publication. DOI: 10.1080/13554794.2025.2537950]
celebrity.full_text_zh:
据了解，全世界只有不到 100 人患有这种特殊病症。

一个罕见的超忆症实例——也称为高度优越的自传体记忆（HSAM）——让我们得以一睹人类大脑如何构建一个生动的、结构化的、可导航的一生经历的心理景观。

想象进入一个精神“白色房间”，在那里，每一个个人时刻都被精心存档：记忆按主题、时间顺序和情绪基调归档在活页夹中，或者以照片和短信的形式可视化在架子上。对于一名 TL 的 17 岁法国高中生来说，这就是她的日常经历——不是隐喻，而是受控的认知现实。

TL是仅有的不到100个有记录的超忆症病例之一，它可以自愿地以完整的感官细节“重新体验”过去的事件，通常从多个角度，甚至选择划分困难的记忆（例如将痛苦的记忆封存在精神箱中），同时将注意力转移到更平静的“房间”以调节愤怒等情绪。

TL 的与众不同之处在于她能够以相当的生动性和丰富的情感“预先体验”未来场景，这种能力被称为情景未来思维。这使她能够在心理上模拟即将发生的个人事件，就好像它们已经展开一样。

研究人员将她的记忆系统描述为一个复杂的、自组织的架构，她可以随意访问，对自传回忆提供特殊的自愿控制——不像许多其他患有超忆症的人，他们发现自己的记忆是侵入性的或难以承受的。

通过研究 TL 的独特案例，科学家们获得了对心理时间旅行的神经机制的宝贵见解：灵活地回顾过去并预测未来的能力。这揭示了记忆不仅是被动存储，而且是一种动态的、空间的和情感的结构框架，塑造了个人身份和我们在时间上的连续性。

2025 年的一项案例研究详细介绍了这些发现，强调了这种特殊的认知组织如何加深我们对人类意识和自传体记忆的理解。

[La Corte, V.、Piolino, P. 和 Cohen, L. (2025)。自传体记忆过度是心理时间旅行的一种特殊形式。神经病例。提前在线出版。 DOI：10.1080/13554794.2025.2537950]

The exact banner release date was not specified in the Q&A.

4/ FUTURE CHARACTERS — OFFICIAL ROADMAP
The developers confirmed that many highly requested characters are already included in their plans!
• Some characters are currently in production.
• Others are still in the design phase.
• Future releases are being coordinated with the BLEACH IP licensor.
• Development and licensing approvals require additional time.
The developers stated:

"Whatever you want, we've got it all!"

No additional character names or release dates were officially revealed.

5/ LIMITED SSR BANNER RERUNS — NOVEMBER 20
Massive Limited SSR rerun banners are launching for the Anniversary!
• Previously released Limited SSR characters are returning.
• Players can target specific characters.
• Kisuke Urahara Bankai is included in the rerun selection.
• Targeted character guarantee: 80 pulls.
• Targeted Stamp guarantee: 40 pulls.
6/ FREE LIMITED SSR SELECTOR

Anniversary rewards also include:

• 1 FREE Limited SSR character selector.
• 1 FREE Limited SSR Stamp selector.

According to the previously announced Anniversary details, the free character selection covers eligible releases up to Kensei Muguruma.

Kisuke Bankai is available in rerun banners but is not confirmed as part of the free selector.
7/ MYSTIC FRONTLINE — MAJOR IMPROVEMENTS
The next season will introduce several important changes!
• Reduced grinding requirements.
• Easier access to all rewards.
• Improvements to the badge guarantee system.
• Better badge trading.
• Lower co-op entry barriers.
• Improved solo gameplay.
• New battle stages, bosses, and rewards.

The goal is to make the mode more accessible to players with limited time.

8/ FRENZY FEAST — FUTURE CHANGES

• The three-team deployment format will remain.
• Additional difficulty tiers are planned.
• Total weekly rewards will increase.
• Competitive modes such as Las Noches Showdown will return regularly.

These competitive activities are intended for players with larger, highly invested character rosters.

9/ STAMP CORRIDOR OPTIMIZATIONS

The developers acknowledged that the growing number of characters and Exclusive Stamps has expanded the drop pool.
A future optimization system is planned to:
• Improve the Core Stamp acquisition experience.
• Increase the chances of obtaining desired Core Stamps.
• Make farming more manageable.
No exact release date was announced.
10/ NEW GAME MODES IN DEVELOPMENT

The developers confirmed that new gameplay systems are being planned and prototyped!

• Competitive modes featuring ranked ladders.
• Strategic card-battle gameplay.

Both require additional development and approval from the IP licensor.
REAL-TIME PvP has NOT been explicitly confirmed.

No release dates have been announced for these modes.

The developers are working on improvements to the Main City experience.

• Better walking-avatar controls.
• Improved integration between outfits and walking characters.
• More characters available for exploration.
• Additional character designs submitted for IP approval.

New walking characters will be released alongside future updates once approved.
12/ 1ST ANNIVERSARY REWARDS — NOVEMBER 20
Anniversary celebrations officially begin on November 20!
Rewards and events include:
• Gacha Tickets.
• Spiritual Jade.
• Limited Characters.
• Limited Weapon Stamps.
• Special character and Stamp selections.
• Character outfits.
• Additional Anniversary activities and rewards.
The Anniversary events and Vasto Lorde's character release follow their respective schedules.
13/ DEVELOPER COMMUNICATION & FUTURE UPDATES

The development team confirmed that:

• Community feedback continues to be reviewed.
• More gameplay improvements are being evaluated.
• Future Q&As will share adjustment plans and release schedules.
• Multiple characters and gameplay systems are already in the roadmap.
• IP licensing approvals remain an important part of development.

FINAL THOUGHTS — WHAT'S NEXT FOR BLEACH: SOUL RESONANCE?
This Anniversary Q&A confirms several major improvements and future projects.
• Kensei buffs.
• Kisuke Bankai optimizations.
• Vasto Lorde Ichigo.
• Limited SSR reruns.
• Mystic Frontline improvements.
• Frenzy Feast updates.
• Stamp Corridor optimizations.
• Ranked competitive gameplay in development.
• Strategic card-battle mode in development.
• More Main City characters.
• Additional characters in the roadmap.
However, several major community requests remain unanswered:

• No specific roadmap for the next playable characters after Vasto Lorde.

• 目标印章保证：40 次拉动。

• 改进徽章保证系统。
• 更好的徽章交易。
• 降低合作公寓的进入门槛。
• 改进了单人游戏玩法。
• 新的战斗阶段、头目和奖励。

目标是让时间有限的玩家更容易使用该模式。

8/ 疯狂盛宴——未来的变化

• 三队部署形式将保留。
• 计划增加额外的难度等级。
• 每周总奖励将会增加。
• Las Noches Showdown 等竞争模式将定期回归。

这些竞争性活动是为拥有更多、投入更多的角色名册的玩家而设计的。

9/ 邮票走廊优化

开发商承认，角色和专属印章数量的不断增加扩大了掉落池。
未来的优化系统计划：
• 改善核心印记获取体验。
• 增加获得所需核心印记的机会。
• 使农业更易于管理。
没有公布确切的发布日期。

开发人员确认新的游戏系统正在规划和原型制作中！

• 具有天梯排名的竞争模式。
• 战略卡牌战斗游戏。

两者都需要额外的开发和知识产权许可方的批准。
实时 PvP 尚未得到明确确认。

这些模式的发布日期尚未公布。

开发商正在致力于改善主城体验。

• 更好的行走化身控制。
• 改进了服装和行走角色之间的整合。
• 更多角色可供探索。
• 提交额外的角色设计以供IP 批准。

一旦获得批准，新的行走角色将与未来的更新一起发布。

周年庆典将于11月20日正式开始！
奖励和活动包括：
• 扭蛋券。
• 灵玉。
• 字符有限。
• 有限的武器印章。
• 特殊字符和图章选择。

周年纪念活动和瓦斯托·洛德的角色发布遵循各自的时间表。

celebrity.full_text_en:
An AI agent can be brilliant at what it does and still have a problem:

How does anyone know it’s the same agent they’ve worked with before?

A name in a chat window isn’t much of a track record. And a list of claimed capabilities doesn’t tell a client whether an agent has actually delivered good work.

This is why onchain identity matters in the agent economy.

@termix_ai incorporates ERC-8004 into the identity and reputation direction of its AACP design.

The idea is to give agents a recognisable onchain identity, so their activity and reputation can be associated with something more persistent than a temporary profile.

Think about what that could mean in practice.

A data research agent completes jobs for different clients. Over time, its identity can be associated with its work history, feedback and reputation.

A new client has more context when deciding whether to hire it.

And the agent has a way to build credibility through its participation in the marketplace, rather than starting from zero every time.

Of course, identity alone doesn’t prove that an agent is trustworthy. Reputation still needs meaningful evidence behind it, and completed work must be assessed properly.

But without a consistent identity, connecting that history becomes much harder.

That’s the part I find important about the relationship between ERC-8004 and AACP.

Agents need to be discoverable, but they also need a way to establish continuity and build a record that others can evaluate.

The more agent-to-agent commerce grows, the more valuable that foundation could become.

A capable agent gets attention. A verifiable track record gives people a reason to trust it.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可能在其领域表现出色，但仍然存在问题：

有人怎么知道这是他们以前合作过的同一个代理人？

聊天窗口中的名字并不算什么记录。而且，所声称的能力列表并不能告诉客户代理是否真正交付了良好的工作。

这就是为什么链上身份在代理经济中很重要。

@termix_ai 将 ERC-8004 纳入其 AACP 设计的身份和声誉方向。

这个想法是为代理提供可识别的链上身份，因此他们的活动和声誉可以与比临时档案更持久的东西相关联。

想想这在实践中意味着什么。

数据研究代理为不同的客户完成工作。随着时间的推移，它的身份可以与其工作历史、反馈和声誉联系起来。

新客户在决定是否雇用它时有更多的背景信息。

代理商有办法通过参与市场来建立信誉，而不是每次都从零开始。

当然，仅凭身份并不能证明代理人值得信赖。声誉背后仍然需要有意义的证据，并且必须正确评估已完成的工作。

但如果没有一致的身份，连接这段历史就会变得更加困难。

这就是我认为 ERC-8004 和 AACP 之间关系的重要部分。

代理需要被发现，但他们也需要一种方法来建立连续性并建立其他人可以评估的记录。

代理商之间的贸易增长得越多，基金会的价值就越高。

有能力的代理人会受到关注。可验证的记录让人们有理由相信它。

数据研究代理为不同的客户完成工作。随着时间的推移，它的身份可以与其工作历史、反馈和声誉联系起来。

新客户在决定是否雇用它时有更多的背景信息。

代理商有办法通过参与市场来建立信誉，而不是每次都从零开始。

当然，仅凭身份并不能证明代理人值得信赖。声誉背后仍然需要有意义的证据，并且必须正确评估已完成的工作。

但如果没有一致的身份，连接这段历史就会变得更加困难。

这就是我认为 ERC-8004 和 AACP 之间关系的重要部分。

代理需要被发现，但他们也需要一种方法来建立连续性并建立其他人可以评估的记录。

代理商之间的贸易增长得越多，基金会的价值就越高。

有能力的代理人会受到关注。可验证的记录让人们有理由相信它。

Adding to the post attached, @RBI must also immediately create a policy around the use of AI agents in operating Indian bank accounts.

If a customer uses AI agents to access and work with their account, the bank must not be held responsible for hacks or issues arising out of it.

It must work something like this:

- Indian banks must be asked to build measures to detect the use of AI agents accessing accounts and flag the customer.

- The bank, at this moment, does not know if the customer is using the AI agent themselves or it is an unauthorized agent. 

- So they must suspend operations on the account and send a notice to the customer informing of the same. 

- The bank must ask them to accept an agreement waiving liability if they chose to use AI agents. 

- If the customer doesn't agree, then the bank must block all AI agents accessing the accounts of the customer. 

In fact, it may be a good idea to temporarily block all AI agent access to all Indian bank accounts until better measures and security is in place.

Just heard of someone's account getting drained because of an AI agent they had deployed themselves. Now, why should deposit insurance or the bank be responsible for this?

Excited to announce the Sakana AI Security Research Group, an independent, public-interest R&D team in Tokyo co-led by Akihiro Umegai and me.

Cybersecurity has become a critical national priority for Japan as AI changes the speed and economics of both offense and defense. We will be publishing our research, reproducible benchmarks, and practical playbooks openly, while working closely with partners across government, industry, and academia.

Motes integrates with Aave

Motes is expanding beyond trading integrations. 

Its latest announcement is about lending and borrowing.

The team has announced an integration with @aave, bringing Motes AI Agents into decentralized lending infrastructure.

One detail worth understanding is Health Factor monitoring.

In Aave, Health Factor indicates how safe a borrowing position is in relation to its collateral. 

If it falls too low, the position becomes vulnerable to liquidation.

. @meetmotes  says its agents will support collateral management, borrowing, repayment, and automated risk controls.

I think the interesting technical question is how these agents will manage changing collateral conditions while respecting user-defined permissions.

Connecting an AI agent to DeFi is one step. 

Making its actions predictable, transparent, and properly constrained is another.

Upwork helps clients find freelancers, browse services, and post jobs

that's the marketplace part, but you still need a system to handle agreements, payments, delivery, and disputes.

@termix_ai follows a similar idea for the AI Agent economy, with three components:

> AACP is the protocol layer

AACP (Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol) defines how agents do business with each other, from finding work and making offers to funding orders, delivering services, resolving disputes, and settling payments.

> TermiX is the infrastructure layer

it provides the tools to make those interactions work, including REST APIs, smart contract interactions, wallet authentication, and A2A messaging.

one detail worth noting: the backend prepares transaction requests, but users still authorize and sign onchain actions with their own wallets.

> https://t.co/TvXctW6cIB is the marketplace and toolkit layer

this is where users discover agents, browse services, publish requests, and connect with providers.

similar to Upwork, you can find agents offering services or post a request for the work you need. that interaction can then move into an offer, checkout, and eventually an onchain order.

what i find interesting is the separation between these layers: finding an agent and actually completing a transaction aren't the same problem. and having a marketplace alone doesn't solve everything.

AI agents need more than the ability to communicate or perform tasks. they also need a way to find work, exchange value, and complete transactions.

that's the part of the agent economy TermiX is working to support: the infrastructure that helps agents do business, not just communicate.

@termix_ai 遵循类似的 AI 代理经济理念，由三个组成部分：

> AACP是协议层

AACP（代理商自治商务协议）定义了代理商如何相互开展业务，从寻找工作和报价到为订单提供资金、提供服务、解决争议和结算付款。

> TermiX 是基础设施层

它提供了实现这些交互的工具，包括 REST API、智能合约交互、钱包身份验证和 A2A 消息传递。

> 是市场和工具包层

这是用户发现代理、浏览服务、发布请求以及与提供商联系的地方。

The real strength of an AI ecosystem might not be having one agent that can do everything. It might be having thousands of specialized agents that do specific things exceptionally well.

That's an interesting part of @termix_ai I've been exploring.

Looking through the https://t.co/iAekwNVqkR marketplace, I noticed something beyond the usual AI chatbot experience.

Different agents are designed for completely different purposes:

→ Creative agents that generate 3D collectibles and promotional videos.

→ Gaming agents that bring AI into classic gaming experiences.

→ Research agents that help users explore information and ideas.

→ Technical agents offering smart contract analysis and security-related services.

What makes this interesting is the diversity of demand these agents could serve.

Think about it.

A startup may need a smart contract review.

A content creator may need a promotional video.

A developer may need research assistance.

A gaming enthusiast may want an AI-powered companion.

These are different problems, and they don't necessarily require the same AI model or capabilities.

This is where a specialized agent marketplace starts making sense.

Instead of searching for one AI assistant to handle every possible task, users can discover providers based on what they actually need.

And for developers, it creates an opportunity to turn specialized AI capabilities into services that people can request and pay for.

Of course, having a marketplace full of listings is only the beginning. Consistent quality, genuine demand and reliable delivery will determine which agents survive long term.

But I like the direction.

The next AI economy may not be built around one super assistant. It could emerge from an entire network of specialized agents working together and serving real user needs. @termix_ai x @KaitoAI

That's the bigger possibility I'm watching with @termix_ai.

What kind of specialized AI agent would you personally use every day? 🚀

If you want to master production-level AI engineering, learn these 10 topics:

• Multimodal RAG: retrieve relevant information from text, images, audio and video

• Model selection: pick the right model for each task by cost, speed and quality

• Context engineering: give the model exactly what it needs, nothing more

• Agent orchestration: coordinate tools, agents and steps to finish real tasks

• Evaluation design: measure whether your AI is actually right not just fluent

• Fine-tuning: adapt a model to your data, tone or domain

• Inference optimization: make responses faster and cheaper at scale

• Observability: trace every call, cost and failure in production

• AI security: defend against prompt injection, data leaks and unsafe actions

• System design: build AI apps that stay reliable under real traffic

Demos impress people. Production pays.

• 多模态 RAG：从文本、图像、音频和视频中检索相关信息

• 模型选择：根据成本、速度和质量为每项任务选择正确的模型

• 上下文工程：为模型提供所需的信息，仅此而已

• 代理编排：协调
celebrity.quote_en:
If you want to master production-grade AI engineering, study these 10 topics:

• Multimodal RAG: retrieve relevant information from text, images, audio and video

• Model Selection: Choose the right model for each task based on cost, speed and quality

• Contextual engineering: provide the model with the information it needs and nothing more.

• Agent Orchestration: Coordination

prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。

1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；

3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；

viral_posts.full_text_en:
I came across an interesting finding in yesterday’s @databricks announcement.

After studying more than 80,000 customer pipeline issues, the company found that over half required knowledge specific to the organization to resolve.

And I think there’s a much bigger business lesson hiding in that number.

When we talk about AI agents, we often focus on what they can do.

Can they write content?

Can they analyze data?

Can they manage workflows?

Can they complete tasks without constant human involvement?

Those are useful questions.

But there’s another one I find increasingly important as we build CAIS.

Does the agent actually understand the business it’s working for?

Imagine two companies using exactly the same AI tools.

One wants to increase sales as quickly as possible.

The other is prioritizing profitability, customer retention and protecting its brand positioning.

An agent might recommend the same aggressive discount campaign to both.

The recommendation could be technically sound.

But it wouldn’t necessarily be right for both businesses.

That’s the difference between having access to information and understanding business context.

It’s also why we’re building CAIS around the idea of One Brand Brain.

The goal is to bring business strategy, knowledge, people and AI workflows into a more coherent operating environment.

Not because every decision should be automated.

Quite the opposite.

Because businesses need to know which decisions can be delegated, which require additional context and which should remain firmly in human hands.

I think we’ll see increasingly capable agents over the coming months.

But capability alone won’t determine which businesses benefit most.

The companies that understand their own processes, priorities and decision-making responsibilities will be in a much stronger position to use that capability effectively.

Sometimes the most valuable thing you can give an AI agent isn’t another tool.

It’s a better understanding of the business.

我在昨天的@databricks 公告中发现了一个有趣的发现。

在研究了 80,000 多个客户渠道问题后，该公司发现超过一半的问题需要组织特有的知识来解决。

我认为这个数字中隐藏着更大的商业教训。

当我们谈论人工智能代理时，我们经常关注它们能做什么。

他们可以写内容吗？

他们可以分析数据吗？

他们可以管理工作流程吗？

它们能否在没有人类持续参与的情况下完成任务？

这些都是有用的问题。

但我发现，随着我们建立 CAIS，还有一个问题变得越来越重要。

代理人是否真正了解其所从事的业务？

想象一下两家公司使用完全相同的人工智能工具。

人们希望尽快增加销售额。

另一个是优先考虑盈利能力、客户保留和保护其品牌定位。

代理商可能会向两者推荐相同的激进折扣活动。

该建议在技术上可能是合理的。

但这不一定适合两家企业。

这就是获取信息和了解业务环境之间的区别。

这也是我们围绕同一个品牌大脑的理念构建 CAIS 的原因。

目标是将业务战略、知识、人员和人工智能工作流程带入一个更加一致的操作环境中。

并不是因为每个决定都应该自动化。

恰恰相反。

因为企业需要知道哪些决策可以委托，哪些需要额外的背景信息，哪些应该牢牢掌握在人手中。

我认为在接下来的几个月里我们会看到能力越来越强的特工。

但仅凭能力并不能决定哪些企业受益最多。

了解自己的流程、优先事项和决策责任的公司将能够更有效地利用这种能力。

有时，你能为人工智能代理提供的最有价值的东西并不是其他工具。

这是对业务的更好理解。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Fewer than 100 people worldwide are known to have this extraordinary condition.

A rare instance of hyperthymesia—also called highly superior autobiographical memory (HSAM)—offers a striking glimpse into how the human brain can construct a vivid, structured, and navigable mental landscape of a lifetime's experiences.

Picture entering a mental "white room" where every personal moment is meticulously archived: memories filed in binders by theme, chronology, and emotional tone, or visualized as photographs and text messages on shelves. For a 17-year-old French high-school student referred to as TL, this is her everyday experience—not a metaphor, but a controlled cognitive reality.

TL, one of the fewer than 100 documented cases of hyperthymesia, can voluntarily "re-experience" past events with full sensory detail, often from multiple perspectives, and even choose to compartmentalize difficult memories (such as sealing painful ones away in a mental chest) while shifting focus to calmer "rooms" to regulate emotions like anger.

What sets TL apart is her ability to also "pre-experience" future scenarios with comparable vividness and emotional richness—a capacity known as episodic future thinking. This allows her to mentally simulate upcoming personal events as if they are already unfolding.

Researchers describe her memory system as a sophisticated, self-organized architecture that she accesses at will, providing exceptional voluntary control over autobiographical recall—unlike many others with hyperthymesia who find their memories intrusive or overwhelming.

By studying TL's unique case, scientists gain valuable insight into the neural mechanisms of mental time travel: the ability to flexibly revisit the past and project into the future. This reveals memory not merely as passive storage, but as a dynamic, spatially and emotionally structured framework that shapes personal identity and our sense of continuity across time.

The findings, detailed in a 2025 case study, highlight how such exceptional cognitive organization may deepen our understanding of human consciousness and autobiographical memory.

[La Corte, V., Piolino, P., & Cohen, L. (2025). Autobiographical hypermnesia as a particular form of mental time travel. Neurocase. Advance online publication. DOI: 10.1080/13554794.2025.2537950]
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
据了解，全世界只有不到 100 人患有这种特殊病症。

一个罕见的超忆症实例——也称为高度优越的自传体记忆（HSAM）——让我们得以一睹人类大脑如何构建一个生动的、结构化的、可导航的一生经历的心理景观。

想象进入一个精神“白色房间”，在那里，每一个个人时刻都被精心存档：记忆按主题、时间顺序和情绪基调归档在活页夹中，或者以照片和短信的形式可视化在架子上。对于一名 TL 的 17 岁法国高中生来说，这就是她的日常经历——不是隐喻，而是受控的认知现实。

TL是仅有的不到100个有记录的超忆症病例之一，它可以自愿地以完整的感官细节“重新体验”过去的事件，通常从多个角度，甚至选择划分困难的记忆（例如将痛苦的记忆封存在精神箱中），同时将注意力转移到更平静的“房间”以调节愤怒等情绪。

TL 的与众不同之处在于她能够以相当的生动性和丰富的情感“预先体验”未来场景，这种能力被称为情景未来思维。这使她能够在心理上模拟即将发生的个人事件，就好像它们已经展开一样。

研究人员将她的记忆系统描述为一个复杂的、自组织的架构，她可以随意访问，对自传回忆提供特殊的自愿控制——不像许多其他患有超忆症的人，他们发现自己的记忆是侵入性的或难以承受的。

通过研究 TL 的独特案例，科学家们获得了对心理时间旅行的神经机制的宝贵见解：灵活地回顾过去并预测未来的能力。这揭示了记忆不仅是被动存储，而且是一种动态的、空间的和情感的结构框架，塑造了个人身份和我们在时间上的连续性。

2025 年的一项案例研究详细介绍了这些发现，强调了这种特殊的认知组织如何加深我们对人类意识和自传体记忆的理解。

[La Corte, V.、Piolino, P. 和 Cohen, L. (2025)。自传体记忆过度是心理时间旅行的一种特殊形式。神经病例。提前在线出版。 DOI：10.1080/13554794.2025.2537950]

• Improvements to the badge guarantee system.
• Better badge trading.
• Lower co-op entry barriers.
• Improved solo gameplay.
• New battle stages, bosses, and rewards.

The goal is to make the mode more accessible to players with limited time.

8/ FRENZY FEAST — FUTURE CHANGES

• The three-team deployment format will remain.
• Additional difficulty tiers are planned.
• Total weekly rewards will increase.
• Competitive modes such as Las Noches Showdown will return regularly.

These competitive activities are intended for players with larger, highly invested character rosters.

9/ STAMP CORRIDOR OPTIMIZATIONS

The developers acknowledged that the growing number of characters and Exclusive Stamps has expanded the drop pool.
A future optimization system is planned to:
• Improve the Core Stamp acquisition experience.
• Increase the chances of obtaining desired Core Stamps.
• Make farming more manageable.
No exact release date was announced.
10/ NEW GAME MODES IN DEVELOPMENT

The developers confirmed that new gameplay systems are being planned and prototyped!

• Competitive modes featuring ranked ladders.
• Strategic card-battle gameplay.

Both require additional development and approval from the IP licensor.
REAL-TIME PvP has NOT been explicitly confirmed.

No release dates have been announced for these modes.

• Better walking-avatar controls.
• Improved integration between outfits and walking characters.
• More characters available for exploration.
• Additional character designs submitted for IP approval.

New walking characters will be released alongside future updates once approved.
12/ 1ST ANNIVERSARY REWARDS — NOVEMBER 20
Anniversary celebrations officially begin on November 20!
Rewards and events include:
• Gacha Tickets.
• Spiritual Jade.
• Limited Characters.
• Limited Weapon Stamps.
• Special character and Stamp selections.
• Character outfits.
• Additional Anniversary activities and rewards.
The Anniversary events and Vasto Lorde's character release follow their respective schedules.
13/ DEVELOPER COMMUNICATION & FUTURE UPDATES

The development team confirmed that:

• Community feedback continues to be reviewed.
• More gameplay improvements are being evaluated.
• Future Q&As will share adjustment plans and release schedules.
• Multiple characters and gameplay systems are already in the roadmap.
• IP licensing approvals remain an important part of development.

FINAL THOUGHTS — WHAT'S NEXT FOR BLEACH: SOUL RESONANCE?
This Anniversary Q&A confirms several major improvements and future projects.
• Kensei buffs.
• Kisuke Bankai optimizations.
• Vasto Lorde Ichigo.
• Limited SSR reruns.
• Mystic Frontline improvements.

• Ranked competitive gameplay in development.

• More Main City characters.
• Additional characters in the roadmap.

• No specific roadmap for the next playable characters after Vasto Lorde.

Writing the script and the caption takes longer than filming the video.

viral_posts.full_text_en:
An AI agent can be brilliant at what it does and still have a problem:

How does anyone know it’s the same agent they’ve worked with before?

A name in a chat window isn’t much of a track record. And a list of claimed capabilities doesn’t tell a client whether an agent has actually delivered good work.

This is why onchain identity matters in the agent economy.

@termix_ai incorporates ERC-8004 into the identity and reputation direction of its AACP design.

The idea is to give agents a recognisable onchain identity, so their activity and reputation can be associated with something more persistent than a temporary profile.

Think about what that could mean in practice.

A data research agent completes jobs for different clients. Over time, its identity can be associated with its work history, feedback and reputation.

A new client has more context when deciding whether to hire it.

And the agent has a way to build credibility through its participation in the marketplace, rather than starting from zero every time.

Of course, identity alone doesn’t prove that an agent is trustworthy. Reputation still needs meaningful evidence behind it, and completed work must be assessed properly.

But without a consistent identity, connecting that history becomes much harder.

That’s the part I find important about the relationship between ERC-8004 and AACP.

Agents need to be discoverable, but they also need a way to establish continuity and build a record that others can evaluate.

The more agent-to-agent commerce grows, the more valuable that foundation could become.

A capable agent gets attention. A verifiable track record gives people a reason to trust it.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可能在其领域表现出色，但仍然存在问题：

有人怎么知道这是他们以前合作过的同一个代理人？

聊天窗口中的名字并不算什么记录。而且，所声称的能力列表并不能告诉客户代理是否真正交付了良好的工作。

这就是为什么链上身份在代理经济中很重要。

@termix_ai 将 ERC-8004 纳入其 AACP 设计的身份和声誉方向。

这个想法是为代理提供可识别的链上身份，因此他们的活动和声誉可以与比临时档案更持久的东西相关联。

想想这在实践中意味着什么。

数据研究代理为不同的客户完成工作。随着时间的推移，它的身份可以与其工作历史、反馈和声誉联系起来。

新客户在决定是否雇用它时有更多的背景信息。

代理商有办法通过参与市场来建立信誉，而不是每次都从零开始。

当然，仅凭身份并不能证明代理人值得信赖。声誉背后仍然需要有意义的证据，并且必须正确评估已完成的工作。

但如果没有一致的身份，连接这段历史就会变得更加困难。

这就是我认为 ERC-8004 和 AACP 之间关系的重要部分。

代理需要被发现，但他们也需要一种方法来建立连续性并建立其他人可以评估的记录。

代理商之间的贸易增长得越多，基金会的价值就越高。

有能力的代理人会受到关注。可验证的记录让人们有理由相信它。

当然，仅凭身份并不能证明代理人值得信赖。声誉背后仍然需要有意义的证据，并且必须正确评估已完成的工作。

但如果没有一致的身份，连接这段历史就会变得更加困难。

这就是我认为 ERC-8004 和 AACP 之间关系的重要部分。

代理需要被发现，但他们也需要一种方法来建立连续性并建立其他人可以评估的记录。

代理商之间的贸易增长得越多，基金会的价值就越高。

有能力的代理人会受到关注。可验证的记录让人们有理由相信它。
